# AI GridWatch — full text for answer engines

Generated 2026-11-26. Site: https://aigridwatch.com. Data license: CC BY 4.0 with
attribution to "AI GridWatch (https://aigridwatch.com)". Rebuilt daily; every number below
was true on the date above.

## What this site is

AI GridWatch tracks the local fight over U.S. data center development: a
sourced registry of moratoriums, bans and pushback actions; project dossiers;
news; analysis; and free negotiation tools for communities. It is not
anti-development. Every claim on the site links to the document it came from.

## Moratorium tracker — headline numbers (as of 2026-11-26)

- 887 data center moratoriums and pushback actions tracked across
  49 states.
- 707 in force today. 84 proposed. The remainder are expired,
  rejected, vetoed or rescinded.
- 887 rows carry a primary source URL and a verification date.
- Tracker: https://aigridwatch.com/moratoriums · Methodology: https://aigridwatch.com/moratoriums-methodology
- Data: https://aigridwatch.com/data/moratoriums.json · https://aigridwatch.com/data/moratoriums.csv
- Change log (RSS): https://aigridwatch.com/changes.xml · Expiring pauses: https://aigridwatch.com/alerts.xml

## How to read the count

- A row is one documented vote by a city council, county board, planning
  commission, tribal government or state legislature to pause, restrict or
  ban data center development: a moratorium, a data-center-specific zoning
  prohibition, a restrictive rezoning, or a state-level freeze.
- "In force" is derived from the recorded end date on the day of the build.
  A moratorium past its documented term shows as Expired; it is never
  reported as current. Rows with no end date declare whether the term is
  standing, condition-based, or simply undocumented.
- Counts differ between public trackers because they count different things
  (proposals vs. enactments, municipalities vs. counties, expired vs. live).
  https://aigridwatch.com/blog/new-jersey-ban-count-2026 works one example.
- One locality, one row. Duplicate events from overlapping research batches
  are merged; multi-locality roundup articles are not treated as duplicates.

## Latest analysis

### A Judge Stopped Google's Virginia Data Center Over a Vote the County Never Described. The Project Is Not Dead.
2026-11-26 — https://aigridwatch.com/blog/botetourt-google-foia-ruling-walk-on-vote-2026
A Virginia circuit judge voided Botetourt County's 2025 deal with Google and ordered construction stopped, because supervisors voted on it after a closed session without saying what it was. The county can hold a proper hearing and vote again. Here is what the ruling says, what it does not, and what to check in your own county's minutes.

### Week in Review: Loudoun County Pauses Data Centers for a Year, Minneapolis's New Rules Die in a Failed Veto Override, and a New York Town's Ban Hits a Legal Snag
2026-11-22 — https://aigridwatch.com/blog/week-in-review-2026-11-22
The country's largest data center market, Loudoun County, Virginia, paused new approvals for 12 months this week — and half a dozen other local governments landed in just as many different places on the same spectrum. Minneapolis's new data center ordinance died when the council fell short of the votes to override a mayoral veto; Rochester, Minnesota banned data centers outright with a 5-1 vote; San Francisco extended its own moratorium for the second time; a New York town's 3-2 vote to ban data centers may not survive a landowner protest petition; and Olyphant, Pennsylvania took a $101 million settlement instead of a fight. Plus: Effingham County, Georgia approved OpenAI's site plan while punting its moratorium decision to January, and Hillsboro, Oregon renewed its pause for a third time.

### Anthropic Went Public With $900 Billion in Compute Commitments. Here Are the Promises It Made to the Towns That Host It.
2026-11-20 — https://aigridwatch.com/blog/anthropic-ipo-900-billion-compute-community-pledges-2026
Anthropic began trading on Nov. 19. Its prospectus discloses about $900.9 billion in commitments, nearly all for compute and data centers, and repeats a pledge to cover electricity price increases its data centers cause. The company has also published commitments on tax incentives, NDAs and community benefit agreements. The prospectus names no sites. One landlord's filing does, in Navarro County, Texas, and its terms are worth reading against the pledges.

### 434 House Races Have a Winner. Only 78 of Them Ever Said Anything Specific About Data Centers.
2026-11-19 — https://aigridwatch.com/blog/house-results-data-center-records-2026
Our House tracker now records a result for every one of the 440 seats on the ballot: 434 winners and six races still in a recount or runoff. Seventy-eight winners have a documented position on data centers. Another 240 are on the record only for one near-unanimous vote. The rest have said nothing we could find, including the new member for the South Jersey district where Vineland sits. What the results show, where they cut against the easy story, and how to look up your own district.

### Nvidia Is Guaranteeing $105 Billion for One Data Center Campus in Pike County, Ohio
2026-11-18 — https://aigridwatch.com/blog/nvidia-118-billion-guarantees-pike-county-ohio-2026
Nvidia's quarterly filing on Nov. 17 shows the chipmaker standing behind $118 billion in guarantees for other companies' data centers. $105 billion of it backs a single site: the PORTS-Pike campus on the old uranium enrichment plant in Pike County, Ohio. What the filing says, what was promised to the county in August, and the state approvals that are still ahead.

### Five Governors-Elect Promised a Data Center Pause. Here Is What a Governor Can Actually Do.
2026-11-17 — https://aigridwatch.com/blog/governors-elect-data-center-moratorium-pledges-2026
Of 34 winning candidates for governor, 32 backed tighter rules on data centers and 12 backed a ban or moratorium, according to a tally cited by the Associated Press. The pledges are real. So are the limits: a governor cannot repeal a tax break alone, cannot freeze a permit already issued, and an executive-order pause may not survive a lawsuit. A state-by-state read of what was promised and which lever it depends on.

### Nine Senate Seats Flipped. Here Is What the Winners Put in Writing About Data Centers.
2026-11-16 — https://aigridwatch.com/blog/senate-results-data-center-promises-2026
All 35 Senate races on the 2026 ballot now have a called winner. Thirteen of those winners left a documented position on data centers during the campaign, and twelve of the thirteen promised some version of the same thing: data centers pay their own way. This post lists who promised what, with the source for each, and what none of it guarantees.

### Week in Review: Minneapolis Passes Data Center Rules But Not a Ban, Oakland Extends Its Moratorium to 2027, and a Third Lawsuit Hits OpenAI's Georgia Project
2026-11-15 — https://aigridwatch.com/blog/week-in-review-2026-11-15
Eight cities and counties landed in eight different places on the spectrum from outright ban to negotiated settlement this week. Minneapolis passed new data center rules but not the ban some residents wanted; Oakland extended its moratorium through 2027; Springfield, Missouri's moratorium survived a developer's court challenge; and a third lawsuit, this one alleging racketeering, hit OpenAI's Project Camellia in Effingham County, Georgia. In North Texas, Fort Worth is still weighing a 90-day pause while neighboring Westlake already settled its way to a cleared project. Plus: a 800-signature petition in Bow, New Hampshire, a second failed moratorium vote in Aurora, Colorado, and a push to block an air permit in South Brunswick, New Jersey.

### Week in Review: Data Centers Lose Nearly Every Ballot Measure Nationwide, Georgia Flips Its Utility Board, and OpenAI Launches a Post-Election Charm Offensive
2026-11-08 — https://aigridwatch.com/blog/week-in-review-2026-11-08
In Tuesday's elections, voters decided data-center ballot measures in roughly ten states and 41 local contests — the industry won one. Ohio's wave of local bans swept through Election Day and cost Vantage Data Centers a project in Oregon, Ohio; Georgia voters flipped control of the state's Public Service Commission; and Texas elected a governor who says she'll keep the state's data center moratorium going. OpenAI responded with a new policy framework promising more local input and a pledge to cover its own power costs. Plus: Bernie Sanders wants a national moratorium, and fresh bans in Maine, Connecticut and New Jersey.

### Week in Review: Charlotte Extends Its Data Center Pause to 2027, Aurora Fails to Ban Them Twice, and a Federal Judge Keeps a Pollution Suit Against Elon Musk's xAI Alive
2026-11-01 — https://aigridwatch.com/blog/week-in-review-2026-11-01
Charlotte's City Council unanimously extended its data center moratorium by 11 months, to October 2027, while Aurora, Colorado failed for the second time in two weeks to even bring a moratorium up for a vote, falling short of the supermajority its own rules require. Davidson County, North Carolina and San Antonio, Texas both rejected moratoriums in favor of permanent rules and case-by-case council approval instead, Pittsburg, California adopted a 45-day pause with a disputed scope, and Oklahoma City approved a rezoning under its own moratorium because the application beat the deadline. Plus: a federal judge refuses to let the Trump administration dismiss the NAACP's Clean Air Act lawsuit against Elon Musk's xAI, and three more fights move in Pennsylvania, Virginia and Iowa.

### Salix, Iowa Says It Has No Data Center Moratorium. It Just Signed a Cost Deal With Google.
2026-10-19 — https://aigridwatch.com/blog/salix-iowa-google-mou-no-moratorium-2026
On Oct. 14 the Salix, Iowa council voted 3-2 to state that no data center moratorium exists, then 3-2 to approve an agreement under which Google pays up to $150,000 for the city's outside advisors. The land has not been sold and no rezoning has been filed. Here is what the agreement does and does not say.

### Week in Review: Oregon's Governor Pauses Data Center Permits Statewide, Milwaukee Bans New Ones for a Year, and a $3 Billion Massachusetts Project Dies on a Technicality
2026-10-18 — https://aigridwatch.com/blog/week-in-review-2026-10-18
Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek ordered state regulators to stop issuing air and water permits for new data centers until mid-2027, and Milwaukee's Common Council unanimously passed its own one-year moratorium. In Texas, Hood County commissioners rejected a developer's settlement offer and permit appeal despite an explicit threat of a lawsuit, while in Massachusetts, a Planning Board quietly killed a $3-4 billion data center campus by refusing to extend a permit the developer let lapse. Plus: Memphis and Shelby County both advance competing moratorium ordinances, a month-old New Jersey diesel spill still hasn't drawn a fine, and West Virginia's governor strikes a deal to relocate a rare 200-tree chestnut grove instead of clearing it.
